meta.title: STF1003 Automatic Tube Feeder vs Manual Tube Feeding | Southern Machinery
meta.description: Interactive 3D model and side-by-side animation: manual tube feeding vs the STF1003 automatic tube feeder. Stacked tubes, stepper-driven spring pusher, fibre sensing, automatic empty-tube ejection. 0.8 s per feed, ±0.5 mm.
meta.keywords: tube feeder, stick feeder, automatic tube feeder, SMT tube feeder, odd-form tube feeder, relay feeder, STF1003, Southern Machinery

hero.h1: Tube-packed parts, fed without a person at the tube.
hero.lead: Relays, terminals, transformers and capacitors arrive oriented in their tubes. What stops the line is the hand that taps, swaps and re-seats those tubes. The STF1003 stacks multiple tubes, pushes parts with a stepper-driven spring, confirms each part by optical fibre and ejects empty tubes on its own.

duel.title: Same tubes, same pick point, two ways to feed them
duel.lead: Left: a tube on a chute, gravity, an operator and a host machine that waits. Right: the STF1003 magazine, spring pusher, fibre check, key and pressing block, and automatic empty-tube ejection.
duel.note: Schematic animation from the STF1003 specification sheet and 3D model. The STF1003 side runs at its published 0.8 s; parts per tube, manual stops and changeover timing are illustrative.

chapters.text: Manual: one tube, gravity, tapping and a tube swap by hand while the head waits. STF1003: stacked tubes, a 57-type stepper driving a spring pusher, optical fibre with software compensation, a positioning key and pressing block, and an air cylinder that drops empty tubes into the recovery box.
One part every 0.8 s at ±0.5 mm, four speed gears, stepper up to 600 rpm.
Multiple tubes stacked; the empty tube is moved aside by an air cylinder and the next one drops in.
PVC or aluminium tubes 200 – 650 mm, wall ≥ 0.6 mm; relays, terminals, transformers, capacitors, DIPs and transistors from 3 to 25 mm.
1350 × 92 × 115 mm, 24 V, 8-core Ø16 mm aviation plug, IO or standalone; installed on Panasonic CM602, JUKI, YAMAHA and Mirae odd-form machines.
1,000 consecutive feeds and 48 hours of continuous operation without abnormality; spring rated for 4 million bends.

why.title: The package is orderly. The handoff is not.
why.lead: Manual tube replenishment and uncertain outlet positioning can interrupt the host machine even when components arrive in an orderly package.

cards.h: Every empty tube is a stop
cards.p: With one tube at a time, each change needs a person and the head waits. A stacked magazine with automatic ejection removes that stop.

cards.h: Orientation is kept, position is not
cards.p: A part can still tilt or jam at the outlet. The STF1003 confirms each part by fibre with software compensation and holds it with a key and pressing block.
DIPs and transistors for screw locking, relays for odd-form insertion, parts for robot cells: one feeding method, one 8-core interface.

blogs.title: Eight engineering reads before your tube-feeding trial

items.title: Know the tube before choosing the feeder
items.summary: Profile, straightness, length and wall decide more than the part does.
body: Measure tube profile, straightness and length on unopened and loaded material. The STF1003 publishes 200 – 650 mm tubes with walls of at least 0.6 mm in PVC or aluminium.
Photograph the tube end and the part spacing before discussing tooling, and send filled and empty tubes with the inquiry.

items.title: Keep the component facing the right way
items.summary: A tube preserves orientation until the outlet; protect it there.
body: Mark the required final orientation on the drawing and follow one sample through the route.
A positioning key and pressing block hold the part at the pick point so the nozzle sees the same pose every cycle.

items.title: Release one part at a time
items.summary: Define double, empty and blocked releases before the trial.
body: Record each failure type separately instead of hiding them in one success figure.
Optical fibre sensing with software compensation confirms each part at the outlet.

items.title: Make the pickup position useful
items.summary: Datum, height and clearance matter as much as speed.
body: Review outlet datum, pickup height, nozzle or gripper clearance and the host-ready signal before agreeing the interface.
The published feeding accuracy is ±0.5 mm.

items.title: Plan for more than one production job
items.summary: Identify which guides need replacement between families.
body: Choose representative jobs rather than assuming one sample covers the range.
Various sizes are available to suit specific site needs; confirm them with samples.

items.title: Make replenishment part of the plan
items.summary: Stacked tubes change who waits for whom.
body: With multiple tubes stacked, the operator loads tubes in batches. Empty tubes leave by air cylinder into the recovery box.
Check access to the magazine and the recovery box at the line, not only on the bench.

items.title: Agree the signal before the bracket
items.summary: IO communication or standalone: decide early.
body: The STF1003 connects through an 8-core 16 mm aviation plug and supports IO communication or self-control without communication.
It runs on 24 V and 0.4 – 0.6 MPa compressed air.

items.title: Ask for a run record, not only a clip
items.summary: 1,000 feeds and 48 hours are the published baseline.
body: The STF1003 is tested for 1,000 consecutive feeds and 48 hours of continuous operation without abnormality.
For your part, agree the acceptance criteria and keep the accepted sample with the production record.
